name: TileLang (Tile Language)
license: MIT (LICENSE also records additional collaboration terms with Microsoft Corporation for 2024-12-01 to 2025-03-14, a window that has passed)
production_evidence: DeepSeek ships TileKernels, a library of kernels written in TileLang, and requires TileLang >= 0.1.15 for it (see flops/tilelang-tile-dsl-moe-routing-quant and the existing kernels source note)
The repo's own dated news records an Ascend 950 backend shipping native code generation - a dependency in DeepSeek's TileKernels requirements rather than a demo
strengths: The 2025-2026 DSL that has actually crossed into a shipped stack - the repo's dated news records DeepSeek depending on it and an Ascend 950 backend with native code generation, automatic scheduling and synchronization (2026-09-30)

Autotuning is built in and correct in the way that matters for deployment: @tilelang.autotune stacked on @tilelang.jit 'compiles candidates in parallel, validates correctness, benchmarks them, and caches the best result for reuse', so tuning is paid once per config rather than per call
Built on TVM, so it inherits TVM's schedule space rather than inventing one
Multi-backend dialect organised over static CUDA, ROCm and Metal (2026-07-24), with a Metal 4 cooperative-tensor GEMM path for Apple M5 (2026-07-28)
Ahead of the curve on block-scaled formats: SM120 NVF4 block-scaled MMA (2026-07-30)
weaknesses: Inherits every TVM dependency and weakness, including the compile-time cost the existing compilers/apache-tvm record documents at minutes to hours with autotuning on
Autotuning costs are real at build time: the config space in the documented example is a product over block_M, block_N, block_K, stages and threads
Younger than Triton with a much smaller deployment base; version 0.1.15 is pre-1.0 and the 0.1.13 notes say several legacy APIs were removed
Pythonic syntax is a lower level of control than Mojo or Triton in the places that matter for peak performance
No AMD MI300-class or Apple production throughput figure is published with methodology - the README shows benchmark plots without conditions
notes: This is the record for 'any 2025-2026 kernel DSL that has become load-bearing', and TileLang is the one that qualified on evidence rather than hype: a shipped kernel library at DeepSeek pins a minimum version of it, and the same repo requires either NVIDIA SM90/SM100 with CUDA >= 13.1 or Ascend 950 with CANN >= 9.2.0. The existing flops/tilelang-tile-dsl-moe-routing-quant record already established the layering - DSL -> kernel library (TileKernels) -> GEMM library (DeepGEMM) - and this record adds the DSL layer the repo's compilers/ type was missing entirely. autotuning is true and the caching behaviour is the deployment-relevant detail: the autotuner benchmarks and caches, so a tuned kernel is reused across launches, which separates it from a search that runs per call. output_artifacts and target_backends both include metal because the repo records a Metal 4 cooperative-tensor GEMM path, not because Metal support is theoretical. compile_time_seconds is null: TVM-based autotuning is measured in minutes to hours per the existing apache-tvm record, which is not a 'typical compile time for a single kernel' and would be misleading here. The README's performance plots are vendor-published without hardware conditions, so no performance figure is asserted in this record; the existing flops record already flags that DeepSeek's 'close to hardware limits' claim carries no numbers.
